subject: Database Management System
intro: Second most-asked subject after DSA. Interviewers probe normalization, ACID, keys, joins, and expect you to write SQL on a whiteboard/notepad — not just define terms.

topics.name: Introduction to DBMS & file system limitations
topics.tip: Say this:data redundancy, integrity constraints, concurrent access, and crash recovery are the 4 things a file system can't give you but DBMS can.

topics.name: 3-Tier Architecture & DBMS Architecture (1/2/3-level)
topics.tip: Trap:"2-tier" = client talks directly to DB (no app server). "3-tier" adds an application layer in between — used in almost every real SaaS backend (like your own PackSage stack).

topics.name: ER Model — entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality
topics.tip: Be ready to draw a quick ER diagram on paper/whiteboard for a simple domain (e.g. "e-commerce orders") — very common OA/interview ask.

topics.name: Types of Keys — Candidate, Super, Primary, Alternate, Foreign
topics.tip: Trap:every candidate key is a super key, but not every super key is a candidate key (super key can have extra redundant attributes). Primary key = the chosen candidate key.

topics.name: Relational Algebra — basic operators (σ, π, ⋈, ∪, −)
topics.tip: Know that SQL is a practical implementation of relational algebra — mapping SELECT→π, WHERE→σ, JOIN→⋈ helps you reason about query optimization questions.

topics.name: Inner Join vs Outer Join (Left/Right/Full)
topics.tip: Trap:LEFT JOIN keeps all rows of the left table even with no match (NULLs on right) — interviewers love asking you to predict output row-count for a given join type + sample data.

topics.name: Join operation vs Nested Subquery — when to prefer which
topics.tip: Joins are generally faster (optimizer-friendly, single pass) vs correlated subqueries that can re-execute per outer row. Good follow-up: "how would you rewrite this subquery as a join?"

topics.name: Normal Forms — 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF
topics.tip: Trap #1 asked topic:memorize the exact difference between 3NF and BCNF — BCNF is stricter (every determinant must be a candidate key, not just handles transitive dependency like 3NF). Be ready to normalize a sample table live.

topics.name: Denormalization — when & why to intentionally break normal forms
topics.tip: Great system-design talking point: denormalize for read-heavy analytics/reporting workloads to cut join costs, at the price of update anomalies.

topics.name: ACID Properties
topics.tip: Trap:Most-asked one-liner. Have a crisp real example ready for each: Atomicity (bank transfer rollback), Consistency (constraints hold), Isolation (concurrent txns don't see partial state), Durability (commit survives crash).

topics.name: Conflict Serializability vs View Serializability
topics.tip: Trap:every conflict-serializable schedule is view-serializable, but not vice versa. Practice drawing the precedence graph — if it has a cycle, the schedule is NOT conflict-serializable.

topics.name: SQL Clauses — WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY
topics.tip: Trap:WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation. Asking you to spot the bug in a query that uses WHERE with an aggregate function is a classic OA MCQ.

topics.name: SQL Queries — practice writing joins, subqueries, window functions
topics.tip: If time is short, prioritize this: write 2nd-highest-salary, department-wise top-N, and self-join queries from memory. These 3 patterns cover ~70% of SQL rounds.

subject: Operating Systems
intro: Broadest core subject — scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, and memory management show up in almost every core-CS + some SDE interviews. Weak OS answers can eliminate you even with strong DSA.

topics.name: Types of Operating Systems (Batch, Time-Sharing, Distributed, RTOS...)
Multiprogramming in OS
topics.tip: Trap:Multiprogramming (keep CPU busy, no time bound) ≠ Multitasking (time-shared, user sees concurrency) ≠ Multiprocessing (multiple CPUs). These 3 get mixed up in MCQs constantly.

topics.name: Real-Time OS (RTOS) — hard vs soft real-time
Process Table & PCB (Process Control Block)
topics.tip: Memorize what fields live in the PCB (process state, PC, registers, memory limits, I/O status) — very commonly asked to "list."

topics.name: Operations on Processes — creation, termination, process states
Context Switching
topics.tip: Be ready to explain context switch overhead and why it's "pure overhead" (no useful work done during the switch itself).

topics.name: CPU Scheduling Algorithms — FCFS, SJF, Priority, Round Robin
topics.tip: OA staple:practice hand-computing average waiting time / turnaround time for a given process table under each algorithm — this shows up as a direct numeric MCQ constantly.

topics.name: CPU Scheduling Criteria (throughput, turnaround, waiting, response time)
Race Condition Vulnerability
topics.tip: Have one concrete real-world example ready (e.g. two threads incrementing a shared counter) and explain why it isn't atomic at the instruction level.

topics.name: Critical Section — the 3 conditions (mutual exclusion, progress, bounded wait)
Types of Semaphores — binary (mutex) vs counting
topics.tip: Trap:a mutex is locked/unlocked by the same thread; a binary semaphore can be signaled by a different thread than the one that waited — this distinction is a favorite "gotcha" question.

topics.name: Producer-Consumer Problem using Semaphores
topics.tip: Be able to sketch the semaphore pseudocode (empty, full, mutex) from memory — this is the single most-drawn diagram in OS interviews.

topics.name: 4 Necessary Conditions for Deadlock (Coffman conditions)
topics.tip: Must memorize verbatim:Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait — breaking ANY one prevents deadlock. Interviewers ask "how would you prevent it" expecting you to map to one of these 4.

topics.name: Banker's Algorithm — safe state check
topics.tip: Practice one full worked example (Allocation/Max/Available matrices → find a safe sequence) by hand — this is a very common written/OA question.

topics.name: Handling Deadlocks — prevention, avoidance, detection & recovery
Paging
topics.tip: Trap:paging removes external fragmentation but can still cause internal fragmentation (last page partially filled). Segmentation is the reverse — know both directions.

topics.name: Page Replacement Algorithms — FIFO, LRU, Optimal
topics.tip: Practice tracing FIFO vs LRU vs Optimal on the same reference string by hand — near-guaranteed OA numeric question.

topics.name: Belady's Anomaly
topics.tip: Trap:Belady's Anomaly (more frames → more page faults) happens with FIFO, but never with LRU or Optimal. This exact fact is a recurring MCQ.

subject: Computer Networks
intro: Less frequent in pure SDE rounds, but a few basic networking MCQs show up in most OAs, and it's core for network/infra-adjacent roles. Focus breadth over depth here.

topics.name: Network Topologies — star, bus, ring, mesh, hybrid
OSI Model (7 layers)
topics.tip: Trap:OSI has 7 layers, TCP/IP has 4-5 (models vary). Know "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away" (Physical–Data Link–Network–Transport–Session–Presentation–Application) cold — asked as a rapid-fire MCQ constantly.

topics.name: MAC Address
topics.tip: Trap:MAC address = physical/hardware, fixed to NIC, works at Data Link layer. IP address = logical, changes, works at Network layer. Classic MCQ pair.

topics.name: IP Addressing — classful addressing
topics.tip: Know how to compute network/host bits and subnet count from a given subnet mask — common OA calculation question.

topics.name: Types of Routing — static, default, dynamic
IPv4 vs IPv6
topics.tip: Trap:IPv4 = 32-bit (~4.3B addresses), IPv6 = 128-bit. IPv6 removes the need for NAT and has no built-in checksum field (relies on lower/upper layers) — a detail interviewers use to check real understanding vs rote memorization.

topics.name: TCP Connection Establishment — 3-way handshake
topics.tip: Highest-frequency CN question:SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK. Also know 4-way termination (FIN, ACK, FIN, ACK) and why TIME_WAIT state exists.

topics.name: UDP — connectionless transport
topics.tip: Trap:TCP is reliable/ordered/connection-oriented (handshake, ACKs); UDP is unreliable/unordered/connectionless but lower latency (used for DNS, video streaming, gaming). Always asked as "why would you use UDP over TCP?"

topics.name: TCP Congestion Control — slow start, congestion avoidance
DNS (Domain Name System)
topics.tip: Be ready to explain the DNS resolution chain: browser cache → OS cache → resolver → root → TLD → authoritative server.

subject: Software Engineering
intro: SDLC models, Agile, COCOMO, requirements, and testing types. Interviewers expect you to know why Agile fits real product teams — connect this back to your own project workflow (DigiFlute internship, hackathons) for a stronger answer.

topics.name: Agile Development Models — Scrum, Kanban, XP
topics.tip: Most-asked SE topic:know the 4 Agile Manifesto values, what a sprint/standup/retro is, and be ready to contrast Scrum (fixed sprints, roles) vs Kanban (continuous flow, WIP limits).

topics.name: Coupling and Cohesion
topics.tip: Trap:good design = LOW coupling + HIGH cohesion. People sometimes flip this under pressure — say it out loud twice before the interview.

topics.name: COCOMO Model — effort/cost estimation
topics.tip: Know the 3 modes: Organic (small, simple), Semi-detached (medium), Embedded (complex, tight constraints) — asked as a straight definitional MCQ.

topics.name: Role & Responsibilities of a Software Project Manager
Classification of Software Requirements — functional vs non-functional
How to Write a Good SRS
Quality Characteristics of a Good SRS
Black Box Testing
topics.tip: Trap:Black box = tests functionality without knowing internal code (you did this for PackSage's 90 endpoints). White box = tests internal logic/paths with code visibility. Don't mix them up under pressure.

topics.name: Integration Testing — big bang, top-down, bottom-up
